app.name: Horizon
app.tagline: Private financial and retirement planning, running on your own machine.
lang.label: Language
home.intro: Model your whole financial life: income, expenses, accounts, debts and milestones such as financial independence or retirement. Your data is stored only on this machine.
home.offer.backtest: Your plan replayed with what markets actually did since 1871, starting in every year of history, and through crises like 1929 or 2008.
home.offer.cashflow: Where your money comes from and goes each year, in a Sankey diagram, with your savings rate, spending by category and the income tax breakdown.
home.offer.finances: Enter by hand who is in the plan, your accounts, income, expenses, debts and early repayments, without linking banks. Includes helpers to estimate your Spanish public pension and health costs by age.
home.offer.plan: A month-by-month projection of your net worth to the end of the plan, with milestones (retirement, financial independence and its variants), Spanish income tax or a flat rate, withdrawal strategies and what you would leave as inheritance.
home.offer.scenarios: Copies of your plan to try other decisions and compare them side by side. Export and import your plans as JSON files.
home.offer.success: Thousands of simulations with random returns to see how likely your money is to last until the end and when you reach your milestones.
home.offer_desc: Six views of the same information. Start with your current finances; everything else is calculated from them.
home.offer_note: Every figure is an estimate for planning, not financial or tax advice.
home.title: Welcome

plan.chart.label: Chart of net worth over the plan, with each account's balance and debts.
plan.col.returns_rate: %s of the starting balance, excluding property

plan.end_value_real: Net worth at the end of the plan, in today's euros.
plan.fail: With these assumptions, the money runs out in %s.

plan.no_accounts: No accounts: add at least one in Current finances to hold what you save.
plan.no_people: To project your plan we need to know how long it lasts: add at least one person with their birth date.
plan.ok: With these assumptions, your money lasts until age %d.
plan.returns_desc: Used for accounts without a return of their own.

plan.shortfall: %s short of covering expenses until age %d.
plan.table.desc_nominal: In each year's euros, not adjusted for inflation.
plan.table.desc_real: In today's euros: every amount is adjusted for expected inflation.

plan.wd_constant: With "%s", once it starts you spend %s of the plan.
plan.wd_range: With "%s", once it starts you spend between %s and %s of the plan (the lowest in %d).
cashflow.intro: Where your money comes from and where it goes each year. Move the year or click a bar in the charts to see it.
cashflow.title: Cash flow
cf.cats_desc: What you spend each year by category, with debt payments in red.
cf.no_income: No income this year: this is what you take from your savings.
cf.rate_desc: How much of your net income you save each year. Red years spend more than they earn; years without income have no bar.
cf.rate_negative: You spend %s more than you earn (%s net).
cf.sankey_label: Diagram of the money flow in %d: income on the left, spending and saving on the right.
cf.shortfall: %s short that not even savings cover.
irpf.even: Withholding covers the tax: the June %d return comes out even.
irpf.paid_now: In June you pay %s from last year's return.
irpf.partial: The plan starts mid-year, so this year's tax return is not computed.
irpf.pay: To pay with the June %[2]d tax return: %[1]s.
irpf.refund: Refunded with the June %[2]d tax return: %[1]s.
irpf.refunded_now: In June you get %s back from last year's return.
irpf.title: Income tax for %d
tax.disclaimer: Taxes are a rough simulation, not an official calculation. The scales and rules may be out of date or contain mistakes, and your real situation (family, deductions, other income) can change the result a lot. For important decisions, check the figures against the Spanish Tax Agency's simulator or a tax adviser.
estate.desc: What is left when the plan ends, in %s, at age %d.
estate.pension_note: Whoever inherits a pension plan pays income tax when cashing it out, as work income.
estate.property_note: Property may also pay the municipal capital gains tax (plusvalía).
estate.tax_note: Inheritance tax is not included: it depends on the region and the relationship.
estate.title: Inheritance
fire.desc: Separate projections that don't change your plan: salaries and self-employment income stop when each financial independence milestone is reached, and from then on you live on your savings and your other income (rent, pensions…).
fire.pension_note: Your plan's public pension is not recalculated: if you stop contributing earlier, it will be lower. You can estimate it again in Public pension.
fire.same: Same as your plan: you already stop working by then
fire.title: If you stop working when you reach FIRE
pension.add_hint: Creates a pension income in 14 payments that starts that month and grows with inflation. You can edit or delete it in Finances.
pension.capped: The pension is limited to the 2025 maximum.
pension.disclaimer: This is a rough estimate, not an official calculation. It assumes your contribution base stays the same in real terms and that you contributed without gaps up to now, and it leaves out special schemes and the transitional choice of the best 27 of the last 29 years. The rules may change. For a reliable figure, use the Social Security simulator with your employment history.
pension.already_retired: %s is already past the ordinary retirement age (%d). If still working, enter the age the pension will start; if already receiving it, add it as an income in Finances.
pension.early_not_allowed: You can't retire that early with those years contributed: it is computed at the ordinary age (%d).
pension.error.not_entitled: There is no pension to add with these figures.
pension.fix_fields: Check these fields to see the estimate:
pension.hint.base: Roughly your gross yearly salary divided by 12. Limited to the 2025 minimum and maximum bases.
pension.hint.regime: For employees, months without contributions in the last 25 years are filled with the minimum base; for the self-employed they are not.
pension.hint.retire: Empty: the ordinary age (65 with 38½ years contributed, otherwise 67). It can be brought forward up to 2 years with 35 years contributed.
pension.hint.topup: Raises the pension towards the minimum when it falls short. Requires other income below a limit.
pension.hint.until: Age at which you stop working (and contributing).
pension.hint.years: Shown in your employment history report (vida laboral). Decimals allowed (e.g. 12.5).
pension.intro: Estimate your Spanish Social Security retirement pension with the rules that apply from 2027 and add it to the plan as income. All in today's euros: pensions are revalued with inflation.
pension.not_entitled: With %s years contributed at retirement you don't reach the 15-year minimum: no contributory pension.
pension.result_lead: %s would receive it from %s, at age %d
pension.title: Public pension
health.empty: Enter an amount to see the total.
health.error.nothing: No band falls within the plan: there is nothing to add.
health.hint: Rough figures in today's euros. Leave the amount empty for anything you don't want to add. Empty “To”: until the end of the plan.
health.intro: Public healthcare covers almost everything, but some costs rise with age: private insurance, the dentist or glasses, and maybe a care home late in life. Adjust the figures and add them to the plan as expenses by age band.
health.title: Health costs
success.intro: Markets do not rise by the same amount every year. Here your plan is replayed with thousands of different return sequences to see how often the money lasts to the end.
success.title: Chance of success
mc.bad_fail: In a bad scenario (1 in 10), the money runs out at age %d (%s).
mc.bad_ok: Even in a bad scenario (1 in 10), you end with %s.
mc.fan_desc: In today's euros. The line is the median scenario; the bands hold the middle half and the middle 80% of scenarios. The dashed line is your plan as the Plan page calculates it, with the expected return every year.
mc.method: Each scenario uses random monthly returns around the expected ones, with each account type's volatility and a 0.6 correlation with the market. In the median scenario each account grows at its expected return, so your plan sits close to the median (a little below it, because good years add more than bad years take away). Inflation stays fixed.
mc.milestones_desc: Milestones that depend on how your investments do, from the best case (1 in 10 scenarios gets there sooner) to the worst (9 in 10 get there sooner).
mc.milestones_title: When you reach your financial-independence milestones
mc.no_conditional: Add a financial-independence (FIRE) milestone in Current finances to see when you reach it in each scenario.
mc.pending: Simulating %s market scenarios for your plan…
mc.settings_desc: How much each account type's return varies from year to year. Expected returns are set in
mc.survival_always: In every simulated scenario you still have money every year until the end of the plan, so there is nothing to draw here.
mc.survival_desc: The share of scenarios that still have money at the end of each year.
mc.survival_title: Chance of having money at each age
mc.verdict: In this share of scenarios, your money lasts until age %d.
backtest.intro: Your plan, replayed with what markets and inflation actually did in the past: the great crises and every start year since 1871.
backtest.title: Historical backtest
bt.crises_desc: Your plan as if each crisis started today, from the market peak before the fall. In today's euros. In the chart, the dashed line is your plan as the Plan page calculates it, with the expected return every year.
bt.crisis_desc.covid: A sharp fall and a fast recovery.
bt.crisis_desc.depression: Stocks fall more than 80% and take decades to recover.
bt.crisis_desc.dotcom: Two big falls in one decade.
bt.crisis_desc.gfc: The 2008 crash, right at the start.
bt.crisis_desc.stagflation: Flat stocks and very high inflation: expenses rise fast.
bt.heat_desc: Each cell is a year in which you could have started your plan. From 1971 the data does not cover the whole plan: those years continue with your expected returns when history ends, and they do not count in the percentage above. Click a cell to see it.
bt.heat_fail: The money runs out at age %s
bt.heat_partial: %s years of historical data; after that, your expected returns.
bt.history_beats_plan: Bear in mind that US stocks returned on average %s a year above inflation, more than the %s your plan assumes for your investments. That is why the past turns out better than the plan: your plan is more cautious than history.
bt.legend_ok: Money lasts (stronger: more left at the end)
bt.method: Data from Robert Shiller (US), %s to %s: stocks with dividends, 10-year bonds and inflation. Investment accounts follow stocks; pension plans 60%% stocks and 40%% bonds; deposits, property and other accounts keep their expected real return on top of historical inflation. Expenses and income that rise with inflation use historical inflation.
bt.partial_starts: From %d to %d, with partial data: %d of %d work out.
bt.sc_fail: The money runs out at age %d (%s).
bt.sc_full: The whole plan uses historical data.
bt.sc_ok: Your money lasts until age %d and you end with %s.
bt.sc_partial: Historical data for %d years; after that, the plan continues with your expected returns and inflation.
bt.verdict: Starting in any year between %d and %d, this share of the time your money lasts until age %d.
bt.pending: Replaying your plan from every year between %d and %d…
bt.worst_fail: The worst year to start was %d: the money runs out at age %d.
bt.worst_ok: Even in the worst year to start (%d), you end with %s.
scenarios.chart_desc: In today's euros, with each scenario's expected returns. The thicker line is the active scenario.
scenarios.col.name: Scenario
scenarios.delete_confirm: Delete this scenario and all its data?
scenarios.error.name: Type a name of up to 80 characters.
scenarios.intro: Copies of your plan to try other decisions (retiring earlier, buying a house) or more cautious assumptions, and compare them. The active scenario is the one you see and edit on the other pages.
scenarios.new_desc: Copy a whole plan to change it without touching the original. The new scenario becomes the active one: edit it in Current finances or Plan and come back here to compare.
scenarios.no_people: No people: add at least one to project this scenario.
scenarios.note: Net worth in today's euros. Chance of success uses 500 random scenarios per plan; the historical test uses the start years with complete data.
scenarios.preset_hint: Pessimistic: returns 2 points lower and inflation 1 point higher. Optimistic: returns 1 point higher.
scenarios.title: Scenarios
import.desc_all: “Export” downloads a plan as a JSON file, and “Export all plans” puts every plan in one file: a backup, or a way to move them to another installation. Importing creates new plans; your existing plans don't change.
import.error.format: This file is not a plan exported from this app.
import.error.invalid: The file has an invalid value in %s (field “%s”). Nothing was imported.
import.error.invalid_named: The file has an invalid value in %s: “%s” (field “%s”). Nothing was imported.
import.error.too_large: The file is too large (2 MB max).
import.error.version: The file comes from a newer version of the app. Update it to import the file.
import.hint: A .json file exported from this app, with one plan or all of them (2 MB max).
import.title: Import a plan
wd.desc: How much you take from your savings each year and from which accounts. With a strategy other than "Planned expenses", your expenses rise or fall (all categories alike) to match what it allows.
wd.hint.fixed: You spend what is planned and take from savings whatever is needed.
wd.hint.guardrails: Like the 4% rule, but you cut 10% if the withdrawal rate rises more than 20% above the starting rate and raise 10% if it falls more than 20% below.
wd.hint.percent: Each year you take that percentage of your savings: you spend more in good years and less in bad ones. The money never runs out, but spending varies.
wd.hint.rule4: In the first year you take that percentage of your savings, then the same amount adjusted for inflation, whatever the markets do.
wd.need_milestone: Choose the milestone the strategy starts at.
wd.no_milestones: First create a retirement milestone in Current finances.
wd.title: Withdrawals in retirement
finances.intro: Where you stand today: who the plan covers, what you own, earn, spend and owe. Type amounts however you like, for example 1,250.50.
finances.title: Current finances
summary.empty: Add your accounts, income, expenses and debts to see where you stand.
summary.label: Summary
summary.note: Before tax. Only counts income and expenses active this month; extra and yearly payments are spread over 12 months.
people.desc: Who the plan covers: you and, if you like, your partner. Birth date and life expectancy set how long the plan runs.
people.empty: Nobody yet. Start by adding yourself.
people.title: People
milestones.desc: Key moments such as retirement or financial independence. Income, expenses and contributions can start or end on a milestone: move it and everything that depends on it moves too.
milestones.empty: No milestones yet. Start with your retirement.
milestones.need_person: Add a person first to create age milestones.
milestones.title: Milestones
milestones.when_fi: Savings of %s times your yearly spending
milestones.when_fi_barista: Savings of %s times what %s a year of part-time work does not cover
milestones.when_fi_budget: Savings of %s times a budget of %s a year
milestones.when_fi_coast: With no more contributions, savings of %s times your spending when %s turns %d
accounts.desc: What you own: current account, savings, investments, pension plans or the value of a home.
accounts.empty: No accounts yet. Add your current account to start.
accounts.title: Accounts
incomes.desc: Money coming in: salary, self-employment, rent or pensions. Gross amounts, before tax.
incomes.empty: No income yet. Add your salary or another source of income.
incomes.title: Income
expenses.desc: Money going out each month or each year. Loan payments go under Debts.
expenses.empty: No expenses yet. Add rent, food or other regular expenses.
expenses.title: Expenses
debts.desc: What you owe: mortgage, loans or cards. From the balance, rate and payment we work out when you finish paying.
debts.empty: No debts. If you have a mortgage or a loan, add it here.
debts.never: The payment does not cover the interest
debts.title: Debts
prepayments.desc: Extra payments to clear a debt early: once, every month or every year. Choose whether to pay less each month or finish sooner. If there is not enough money that month, whatever is available is paid.
prepayments.empty: No early repayments. Add an extra payment to see how much sooner you finish.
prepayments.need_debt: Add a debt first to repay it early.
prepayments.title: Early repayments
contrib.always: While there is money left over
field.debt_redirect: Once paid off, the instalment goes to
field.name: Name
field.prepay_redirect: If the debt is already paid off, the payment goes to
hint.amount_payment: What you receive or pay each time, not the monthly average.
hint.coast_age: The age at which you want to reach FIRE without contributing more.
hint.contrib_until: Contributions stop when the milestone arrives.
hint.contribution: What you add to this account each month.
hint.debt_balance: What you still owe, without future interest.
hint.debt_redirect: From the next month, what you paid each month is added to this account if there is money left over.
hint.fi.barista: Your savings cover what a part-time job does not pay.
hint.fi.coast: You can stop saving: what you already have, growing at the expected return, reaches FIRE by the target age.
hint.fi.fat: Your savings cover a generous budget, higher than what you spend now.
hint.fi.lean: Your savings cover a frugal budget, lower than what you spend now.
hint.fi.standard: Your savings cover everything you spend now.
hint.fi_amount: In today's euros; rises with inflation.
hint.fi_multiple: Reached when your savings, excluding property, hit this multiple of what you spend in a year. 25 is the 4% rule.
hint.growth: Leave empty to rise with inflation.
hint.inflation: Raises income and expenses that follow inflation, and converts to today's euros.
hint.life_expectancy: The age you want the plan to reach.
hint.mc_runs: More scenarios give a steadier result but take longer.
hint.pension_from: Before that milestone nothing is taken from the pension plan. Withdrawing contributions older than 10 years is not modelled.
hint.prepay_amount: What you repay each time, not counting the fee.
hint.prepay_fee: Percentage of the amount repaid. Spanish law caps it, for example at 0.25% on variable-rate mortgages in the first years.
hint.prepay_redirect: Payments due after the debt is gone are sent to this account.
hint.prepay_when: For a single payment, the month you make it. For regular payments, when they start (empty: now).
hint.rate: The nominal rate in your contract.
hint.return: Leave empty to use the default return for this account type.
hint.surplus: What is left each month, after contributions.
hint.tax_es: 2025 Spanish income tax (IRPF) with brackets indexed to inflation, Social Security contributions, monthly withholding and the tax return in June. Simplified: individual filing, no children or regional deductions, self-employment as net profit, joint assets split 50/50 and starting balances with no unrealised gains.
hint.tax_flat: A fixed share of gross income. Simple, but it ignores income types and brackets.
hint.tax_rate: Average effective rate on gross income.
hint.tax_region: Changes the regional half of the general scale. “State” uses the same scale as the State.
hint.wd_ceiling: The most you would spend, as a share of the plan.
hint.wd_floor: The least you would spend, as a share of the plan.
hint.wd_order: When money is short, accounts are drawn in this order. Property is never sold.
hint.wd_rate: Share of your savings (not counting property).

form.error.future: The date cannot be in the future.
form.error.max_people: A plan covers at most two people.
form.error.range: This value is outside the allowed range.
form.error.stale: A person or milestone in this form no longer exists. Check the options and save again.
